fixed_constraints: Retirement deletes 25 wholly predecessor root files, dead symbols in lsp.go and main.go, every retired std/sketches source on the I43 deletion list, and all superseded-contract tests, while current internal packages keep exact semantics free of compatibility flags or fallback parsers.

Surviving launcher commands are assert, build, run, parse, inspect-project, inspect-types, runtime-check, catalogue-check, version, lsp, and clean; explain, lint, baseline, and normalize are cut for executing predecessor parsing, checking, evaluation, or proving.
No external users exist, so backwards compatibility and deprecation windows are non-requirements for cut commands; I45 restores release gates and I50 restores documentation coherence.

The task closes on clean-checkout Go tests, current Can builds, strict emitted TypeScript, staged release tests, explicit rejection of predecessor syntax, and a reviewable deletion list with replacement evidence.
common.purpose: Determine the three open I44 design points for Can retirement: the destiny of removed launcher command names, the demonstration that legacy paths are extinct, and the destiny of the committed-golden TypeScript gate.

residual_proof.background: Post-deletion, I44 must evidence predecessor extinction through static gating of the source tree, behavioral probing with dispatch searches, or a pairing of both.
facts: A reachability sweep from surviving dispatch roots strands every predecessor parser, checker, evaluator, prover, and Z3 symbol unreached, offering a static gate a crisp invariant to lock in.
Predecessor syntax already fails explicitly via current-parse fixtures, while tree searches can attest that Z3, extern-grant, and legacy dispatch vacated the launcher.
A static gate may slide toward allowlist maintenance whereas probes may skip over unreachable-yet-present code, so each route blinds a spot the other illuminates.

retired_command_ux.background: Names of four cut commands outlive their implementations across scripts, notes, and reflexes, demanding loud failure for stale calls rather than quiet success.
facts: Traceless cutting drops explain, lint, baseline, and normalize onto the generic usage error at exit 2, costing zero code and pretending the names never lived.
One stub per name exits 2 with a retired message, orienting stale callers at the price of inscribing four dead names forever in the launcher shed of them.
Withdrawn lsp --baseline already fails with a retired-flag exit-2 error from I41, establishing explicit retirement errors as an existing codebase idiom.

tscheck_fate.background: Strict typechecking of committed .ts goldens under std and sketches flows through tscheck and tsc.yml, whose covered files all vanish in this task.
facts: The gate currently fails over predecessor rot via missing modules and tag-type mismatches, so removal eliminates failing subjects instead of damaging a green signal.
An includes set matching zero files makes tsc fail on absent inputs, hence the existing configuration cannot survive retirement unchanged.
Fresh-emit CI output becomes the TypeScript gating basis under I45 item 2, whether by adapting retained tscheck files or by recreating them post-deletion.
